Abstract
                                                        We consider a many-body Hilbert space with a fixed global charge and show that the
                                                    typical entanglement entropy of a subsystem, at the leading and subleading order in the
                                                    thermodynamic limit, can be expressed in terms of a single quantity which represents the
                                                    local thermal entropy at fixed charge density. We find a general formula which applies
                                                    both to abelian U (1) symmetry and non-abelian SU (2) symmetry, including the case of
                                                    a local Hilbert space which transforms under a general reducible representation of the
                                                    symmetry group. We illustrate the general formula with model systems and discuss the
                                                    relevance of the results as a probe of quantum chaos for physical Hamiltonians.

1        Introduction
In a seminal paper [1] Page showed that, in a N -qubit system with N ≫ 1, the typical
entanglement entropy of a NA -qubit subsystem scales as log(2)NA for NA < N/2. The
coefficient log(2) can be understood as the entropy of a single qubit at infinite temperature.1
    For a system of N qubits at fixed U (1) charge m, the typical entanglement entropy with the
charge constraint [2] is found to scale as η(s)NA , with s = m/N and η(s) = − 1−2s      1−2s
                                                                                 2 log( 2 )−
1+2s      1+2s
  2 log( 2 ), [3, 4]. In this paper we uncover the thermodynamic interpretation of the
function η(s) and show that it can be understood as the local thermal entropy of the one-
body system at fixed average charge. We find a general formula which applies both to the
case of U (1) abelian charge and SU (2) non-abelian charge [5]. The function η(s) is fully
determined by the structure of the local one-body Hilbert space Hloc [6] and its decomposition
into irreducible representations of the local symmetry group. It is given by the expression

η(s) = log(k) − D(ps ∥p⊛ ) ,                                       (1)

where k is the dimension of Hloc , the probability distribution ps is the thermal distribution at
fixed average charge s, the probability distribution p⊛ is the thermal distribution at infinite
temperature, and D(ps ∥p⊛ ) is the relative entropy, or Kullback-Leibler divergence. When
the infinite-temperature distribution p⊛ is the uniform distribution 1/k, the local entropy
η(s) reduces to the Shannon entropy of ps . To our knowledge, the formula (1) and the
thermodynamic interpretation of the function η(s) are new. We show that this general result
allows us to express subleading terms of order O(N 0 ) in the typical entanglement entropy in
terms of the temperature and the local heat capacity [7] associated to the local entropy η(s),
and extends the known expressions for U (1) [2–17] and SU (2) charges [5, 18–22].
    The results presented here are related to a substantial body of literature. The notion
of Page curve for random states without constraints was first introduced in [1]. The exact
formula for the average and variance of the entanglement entropy in the presence of constraints
was derived in [2]. In the case of non-abelian symmetries, group-invariant subsystems at fixed
charge can be defined in terms of subalgebras of observables [23–26]. The exact formula for
the average and the variance of the entanglement entropy for these subsystems was derived

    The paper is organized as follows: In Sec. 2 we introduce the general structure of many-
body systems and introduce the relation between the local entropy η(s) and the asymptotics
of the dimension of the Hilbert space at a fixed global charge. In Sec. 3 we discuss the
decomposition of the many-body Hilbert space at fixed charge into subsystems, and determine
the asymptotics of the dimensions of the subsystems. In Sec. 4 we derive the general formula
for the average entanglement entropy and its variance, which then specialize to the case of
U (1) charge in Sec. 5 and SU (2) charge in Sec. 6. Finally in Sec. 7 we discuss the relevance
of these results for the entanglement entropy in eigenstates of physical Hamiltonians.

7     Discussion
The analysis presented in this paper provides a general treatment of typical entanglement
entropy for any many-body system with a fixed global charge and a general local Hilbert
space Hloc , in the thermodynamic limit N → ∞. The known results on typical entanglement
entropy ⟨SA ⟩N s with fixed abelian and non-abelian charge are recovered as special cases of
the general formula (58):
• In the case of fixed abelian U (1) charge, the average entanglement entropy (58) reduces to
    the expression (73) found in [6] for k-dimensional local Hilbert spaces with particle-number
    conservation, and in [3] for the special case of systems of qubits.
• In the case of fixed non-abelian SU (2) charge,        the average entanglement entropy (58)
    reduces to the expression (108) for general k-dimensional local Hilbert spaces, generalizing
    the result of [5, 20] for the special case of systems of qubits.

The construction presented here applies to any many-body system with a local single-charge
symmetry group and a fixed global charge. We showed that the typical entanglement entropy
admits a thermodynamic interpretation in terms of the local entropy η(s) defined in (11),
where the charge density s plays the role of the energy density of the local system. The
function η(s) is fully determined by the structure of the local Hilbert space Hloc and its de-
composition into irreducible representations of the local symmetry group. It is given by the
expression η(s) = log(k) − D(ps ∥p⊛ ), (11), where k is the dimension of Hloc , the probability
distribution ps is the thermal distribution at fixed average charge s, the probability distri-
bution p⊛ is the thermal distribution at infinite temperature, and D(ps ∥p⊛ ) is their relative
entropy, or Kullback-Leibler divergence. When all local multiplicities are trivial (aqloc = 1),
the infinite-temperature distribution p⊛ = 1/k is uniform, and η(s) reduces to the Shannon
entropy of ps . To our knowledge, the formula (11) and the thermodynamic interpretation of
η(s) are new.
    Starting from the thermodynamic interpretation of the charge density s as local energy
and the function η(s) as local entropy, we defined the inverse temperature β∗ (s) = η ′ (s) and
the local heat capacity c∗ (s) = ∂s/∂(β∗−1 ). The infinite-temperature limit β∗ (s⊛ ) = 0 defines
the critical charge density s⊛ . With these definitions, we can characterize the behavior of the
average entanglement entropy ⟨SA ⟩N s in thermodynamic terms:

• At the leading order O(N ) and up to half-system size f ≤ 1/2, the average entanglement
    entropy is extensive, i.e., it is proportional to the number NA of bodies in the subsystem
    A. The coefficient of the leading order term is the local entropy η(s) defined in (11) and
    described above, (1). In the case of local qubit Hilbert space (k = 2), we find that the
    expressions (78) and (113) for fixed global U (1) charge m (with s = m/N ) and global SU (2)
    charge j (with s = j/N ) have the same form ηU (1)−qubit (s) = ηSU (2)−qubit (s) and match the
    expressions found in [2–22]. In the case of local qutrit Hilbert space (k = 3), we find again
